first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation while supporting durable time-to-value. Verify memory_86 for adoption and downstream-quality evidence, and memory_73 to determine whether promotional pricing produced sustainable qualified revenue rather than acquisition lift driven by discounts. Pricing remains a credible alternative, but margin, retention, and customer-quality effects are not stated in the consolidated memory.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the onboarding flow. The verified source directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, aligning with sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its verified cohort had 30-day retention down 12% and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Measure completion, first meaningful action, time-to-value, retention, and qualified revenue before considering rollout.
